findings.claim: The Surreal projection implementation returns `Ok(false)` from a function whose signature returns `Result<ProjectionApply, PortError>`, so the workspace will not compile.
findings.evidence: In the added `async fn apply(...) -> Result<ProjectionApply, PortError>` hunk, the cursor check branch contains `if !cursor_advances(checkpoint, &cursor)? { return Ok(false); }`; constraint R1 requires `cargo check --workspace` to be clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Return `Ok(ProjectionApply::Duplicate)` or the appropriate `ProjectionApply` variant instead of `Ok(false)`.

findings.claim: A slow snapshot consumer can block forever without receiving terminal `Lagged`, violating the bounded-buffer/slow-client lag acceptance requirement.
findings.evidence: Acceptance task 4 requires slow-client lag to meet the contract; `run_producer` sends all `initial` snapshot frames with `tx.send(frame).await` before entering the live loop, while `Lagged` is emitted only later on `tx.try_send(frame)` failure in the live-delivery path.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same non-blocking bounded send policy for initial frames, emitting terminal `Lagged { checkpoint_resumable: false, ... }` when the initial queue fills.

findings.claim: Subscribe permission revocation can still race a queued protected mutation because delivery does not recheck subscription authority immediately before enqueueing or before output.
findings.evidence: The producer checks `producer.authz.check(&producer.subscribe_tuple)` only on the periodic `interval.tick()` branch, but after `raw.next()` it authorizes only the object tuple and then enqueues `EntityTypeWatchFrame::Mutation` with `tx.try_send(frame)`; `next_output` only consults `terminal_rx` and performs no fresh authority check before returning queued frames. Acceptance task 4 requires revocation to meet the contract.
findings.suggested_fix: After receiving and object-authorizing a protected delivery, recheck the subscription tuple immediately before enqueueing; also ensure any revocation signal preempts already queued protected frames before client delivery.
